name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Gary Palmer running with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: Palmer holds a deep-red Birmingham-area seat with a 17-point partisan lean and a massive financial advantage, while Mercer's campaign is essentially unfunded. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold.
model.watch: A surprise national Democratic wave or an unexpected Palmer scandal would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gary Palmer is seeking another term in Alabama's 6th District, a Birmingham-area seat that leans Republican by about 17 points. He has raised over $1 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic challenger Maurice Mercer has raised only a few thousand dollars and shows no outside support. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Palmer roughly a 96 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals align with the district's lean: incumbency and the money gap both favor Palmer, and there is no evidence of a competitive environment here. The race is rated Safe R, with the main uncertainty limited to turnout variation rather than a genuine contest.
